title: Pranav's GTM Agent - design rationale
purpose: Machine-readable companion to the README: why the agent is shaped this way, what it runs on, and how it grades itself. Written against the five questions any evaluation of an agent like this asks.

does_the_agent_work.claim: Point it at any competitor in or adjacent to Rippling's space and it produces an evidence-graded brief plus a claims ledger where every quote re-verifies against the live web.
proof: outputs/ holds six eval-passed audits: Gusto, BILL (x2), Deel, Ramp, Justworks, BambooHR
Deel run: 43/43 measured quotes re-found verbatim on live pages by the grounding checker
LLM judge (a 'demanding Rippling VP of Growth' rubric) scored the Gusto, BILL and Deel briefs 5/5 overall
Two research rounds per audit are typical; the master self-corrected a wrong round-1 conclusion on Deel after round-2 evidence contradicted it

architecture_quality.claim: A real decision-making loop, not a pipeline: the master chooses lanes per competitor, sharpens per-researcher focus, routes failures, decides when a second round is worth it, and declines work that will not change conclusions.
proof: Observed live: master declined a third research round on Deel stating no strategic conclusion was waiting on more evidence
Goal-discovery intake: before spending, it asks (with defaults) what the audit feeds, which product motion matters, and which hypotheses to pressure-test - answers become per-lane focus notes
Checkpoint walk: research runs fully parallel, then findings are presented as five interactive stops where the user can dig into the live ledger before the report exists

tool_usage.claim: Right tool per job, and every source failure is routed, never surfaced as an error or silently swallowed.
proof: Each ads researcher works a four-tier source ladder (official ad libraries -> ad-spy aggregators -> ad landing pages -> pixel/traffic/hiring signals) and drops down it automatically when walled
Coverage gaps are disclosed exactly once, honestly, in the brief's section 8 - with the fallback that was used
Live example: Meta Ad Library renders empty to automated fetches; the run recorded it, fell back to third-party libraries, and a rendered-browser retry later captured the measured creative set

output_quality.claim: The brief is campaign-ready, and section 7 (Rippling gaps and opportunities) is anchored to cited claims rather than generic advice.
proof: Structural eval requires >= 5 citations inside the Rippling section alone; recent runs carry 60+
Section 7 pairs declared strategy vs actual buyer demand (what their ads say vs what buyers complain about), names segments and channels, ends with a citation-anchored kill sheet
Every claim carries a verbatim quote, URL, timestamp, evidence grade, and verification state; the claims ledger ships as JSON plus a filterable HTML report

decisions_and_tradeoffs.claim: Every major choice below records the tradeoff accepted alongside the reason.

architecture_decisions.why: The agentic loop IS the product. A framework would hide exactly the decisions worth seeing: which lanes to run, how to route failures, when to stop. ~700 lines of visible Python means every decision point is auditable.
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: No framework conveniences (retries, tracing come hand-rolled).

architecture_decisions.decision: Formation, not pipeline: master -> five parallel lane researchers -> adversarial verifier -> brief writer
architecture_decisions.why: Research is parallelizable and needs materially different context per lane (different playbooks, sources, budgets); judgment is not parallelizable and needs one owner. Rule: parallelize sources, never judgment. Verification must live in a fresh context because a context that generated claims will defend them.
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: Coordination overhead and compressed handoffs - mitigated by making the handoff artifact structured data (the ledger with verbatim quotes), never prose summaries.

architecture_decisions.decision: Claims ledger as the spine: append-only rows with ID, verbatim quote, URL, timestamp, evidence grade (measured / stated_by_competitor / proxy / inferred), verification state
architecture_decisions.why: The brief cites claim IDs inline so every sentence is auditable back to a URL. The ledger doubles as session state (follow-ups reuse it instead of re-researching) and as longitudinal memory (dated JSONs in git; re-runs auto-diff against the prior run to answer 'what changed').
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: Claims regenerate IDs each run, so cross-run matching uses stable evidence (URLs, quote fingerprints) instead of IDs.

architecture_decisions.why: The same competitor audit should be shaped differently for campaign plays vs a sales battlecard vs an exec readout. One message, at most three defaulted questions; 'standard sweep' skips. Answers travel into lane focus notes and the brief's section 7 emphasis.
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: One extra conversational turn before research starts.

architecture_decisions.why: The public web actively resists automated reading (JS walls, 403s, 404s) - every single run hit 3-5 blocked sources. Researchers auto-descend a source ladder and keep partial reads; the master never surfaces plumbing to the user; gaps are disclosed once in section 8 where they belong. Without this, briefs read confident while whole evidence categories are missing.
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: Some fallback reads are proxy-grade - which is why grades exist and confidence is capped accordingly.

architecture_decisions.why: Marketing intel dies stale: pricing, homepage messaging and active ads change weekly, and 'what changed recently' is a required output. Retrieval is the live web at run time, steered mid-run by the master; grounding is the whole ledger in context (cross-lane synthesis needs the full picture, not top-k chunks); provenance must re-verify against live pages.
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: No cross-session semantic search; longitudinal memory is the dated-ledger diff instead.

architecture_decisions.decision: Verification enforced in code, not by prompt
architecture_decisions.why: Under speed pressure the master once sampled 14 of 101 claims for verification and went to print - the eval harness caught it (13% pass-rate). Now write_brief itself auto-verifies anything unjudged before writing. Judgment gets a gate, not a suggestion.
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: A brief written after a huge multi-round ledger pays a verification delay it cannot skip.

architecture_decisions.decision: One Session, three frontends (CLI, web chat, resumable brand threads)
architecture_decisions.why: The Session emits structured events; the CLI prints them, the web UI renders them as live cards, and brand threads reload prior conversation plus the brand's ledger so follow-ups continue with full context. One loop means a behavior fixed once is fixed everywhere, and the reviewer can literally watch decide -> dispatch -> verify happen.
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: Server keeps in-memory named sessions; process restart drops live threads (their transcripts and ledgers persist on disk and re-seed).

architecture_decisions.why: Wanted conversational pacing without wall-clock cost: all five researchers fire in parallel as usual, then findings are walked one lane at a time with 'dig in or continue?' stops answered from the live ledger. Interaction layer, not an execution layer.
architecture_decisions.tradeoff_accepted: Checkpoint stops add user-paced latency to the final report when enabled - by design.

tool_and_model_choices.choice: Claude Opus for judgment, Sonnet for extraction
tool_and_model_choices.what: Master, adversarial verifier, brief writer and LLM judge run the flagship; the five lane researchers run claude-sonnet-5 at capped claim volume (max 18/lane).
tool_and_model_choices.why: Researchers execute tight playbooks - a faster model loses little there and cut lane wall-time roughly in half; synthesis, adversarial verification and section-7 judgment are where model quality shows. Both overridable via env (LANE_MODEL, JUDGE_MODEL, AGENT_MODEL).
tool_and_model_choices.tradeoff: A faster researcher over-produced claims at first (38 in one lane); fixed with schema-enforced caps because every claim costs verification downstream.

tool_and_model_choices.choice: Server-side web_search + web_fetch as the research tools
tool_and_model_choices.what: Anthropic's server tools with per-lane max_uses budgets; seed URLs injected per lane (ad libraries, pricing pages, archives, pixel/traffic lookups).
tool_and_model_choices.why: Zero scraping infrastructure for a reviewer to install, budgets enforced server-side, dynamic content filtering built in.
tool_and_model_choices.tradeoff: JS-heavy surfaces (ad libraries) may render empty - handled as first-class coverage reporting plus the source ladder, and a rendered-browser pull is the documented escalation rather than a bundled headless-browser dependency.

tool_and_model_choices.what: api: Anthropic API with schema-validated structured outputs, prompt caching, pause_turn resume, backoff. cli: every model call becomes a `claude -p` subprocess billing a Claude subscription - zero API key.
tool_and_model_choices.why: Reviewers without an API key can run everything (the entire sample set was produced keyless). The CLI master loop is a JSON action protocol - still decide -> execute -> observe - hardened against transcript echo with a last-action parser, an anti-replay check, and one corrective retry.
tool_and_model_choices.tradeoff: CLI runtime pays a cold-start tax per master decision (~30-60s each) and budgets become prompt instructions instead of hard server caps. Stated in the README.

tool_and_model_choices.what: Researcher, verifier and judge responses are schema-validated JSON at the API layer.
tool_and_model_choices.why: No parse-and-pray: malformed output retries at the source instead of poisoning the ledger.
tool_and_model_choices.tradeoff: The cli runtime approximates this with defensive parsing plus one retry.

tool_and_model_choices.what: Five researchers in threads (wall ~= slowest lane, ~2-3 min); the verifier chunks the ledger (24 claims/reviewer) and runs chunks in parallel with an automatic lower-concurrency retry for chunks that fail under load.
tool_and_model_choices.why: Cut a ~13-15 minute audit to ~6-8 minutes of formation work without touching judgment quality.
tool_and_model_choices.tradeoff: Parallel verifiers under heavy load can rate-limit - hence the retry round, and unjudged claims are reported rather than silently passed.

tool_and_model_choices.choice: FastAPI + SSE + a single-file vanilla web UI
tool_and_model_choices.what: server.py streams the Session's structured events; ui/index.html renders chat, live formation cards, checkpoint tracker, audit history and resumable threads with no build step.
tool_and_model_choices.why: A reviewer can read the whole frontend in one file; SSE fits a one-way event stream better than websockets.
tool_and_model_choices.tradeoff: Single-user by design (one flight lock); fine for the tool's purpose.

tool_and_model_choices.what: Every run records lane seconds, verify wall, brief wall and formation total into run.timings inside the claims JSON; the UI shows per-lane seconds live.
tool_and_model_choices.why: Speed regressions should be argued from receipts, not vibes - and slow now fails evals like a quality bug.

eval_system.philosophy: The same adversarial pressure the verifier applies to researchers, the harness applies to the whole agent. Nothing lands unverified; nothing ships uneval'd; every post-eval correction is logged inside the deliverable (run.post_eval_corrections) so the audit trail shows the harness catching things - which is the proof it works.

layers.name: Structural (free, deterministic, CI-ready exit code)
checks: every non-inferred claim carries a verbatim quote
source_url must be a real fetchable URL (aggregate reads are graded inferred)
>= 15 distinct claim IDs cited; zero dangling citations
latency budgets: slowest lane <= 300s, verify <= 300s, brief <= 300s, formation <= 750s

layers.name: Grounding spot-check (network, no LLM)
checks: re-fetch measured claims' URLs with a browser-grade UA
fuzzy-match stored quotes against live page text (5-word shingles, >= 60% must hit)
normalizations learned from real false-fails: html entity unescape, typographic quotes/dashes, tag-strip punctuation spacing
layers.purpose: The anti-hallucination tripwire: a quote that is not on the page fails loudly.

layers.name: LLM judge (one model call)
checks: a 'demanding Rippling VP of Growth' scores 1-5 on evidence-grounding, specificity, recency, and Rippling-actionability
named weaknesses are returned and treated as a fix list, not commentary

logic_flow: 1. run completes -> brief.md + claims.json + claims report .html land in outputs/
2. structural checks run (free) - format, citation, quote, verification-coverage and latency budgets
3. grounding re-fetches a sample (or all) measured quotes against the live web
4. judge reads brief + ledger and returns scores plus named weaknesses
5. every finding becomes a correction: re-grade, re-verify, or fix the harness itself
6. corrections are appended to run.post_eval_corrections inside the claims JSON
7. evals re-run to green before the run is considered closed
8. tests/test_latency.py proves dispatch/verify parallelism and timing persistence with a stub model - zero tokens, CI-ready
track_record: caught composite multi-fragment quotes stitched with ellipses -> replaced with single contiguous verbatim runs
caught proxy fee claims over-graded as 'confirmed' whose source platform 403s direct fetches -> downgraded to plausible
caught the master sampling 14/101 claims for verification under speed pressure -> verification now enforced in code at write_brief
caught placeholder source URLs ('search_snippet_aggregate') -> protocol now requires fetchable URLs, aggregates route to inferred
caught a repair script renumbering claim IDs and dangling five brief citations -> IDs recovered from the git snapshot, repairs preserve IDs
caught its own harness false-failing on bot-walled pages, html entities and curly quotes -> grounding checker hardened, root-caused against live pages

end_to_end_logic_flow: 1. user names a competitor (checkpoints on or off)
2. master scopes the goal: one message, three defaulted questions (end goal / motion scope / hypotheses); 'standard sweep' skips
3. master dispatches all five lane researchers in parallel, each with a sharpened focus note, per-lane budgets, and an 18-claim cap
4. researchers work their source ladders, auto-descending on walls; claims land in the append-only ledger with quotes, grades, timestamps
5. master reads the coverage report and decides: deepen a lane, run a second round, or proceed - never surfacing plumbing to the user
6. (checkpoint mode) findings walked five stops at a time, dig-ins answered from the live ledger, blind progress tracker on the side
7. adversarial verifier attacks every claim in parallel chunks with retry; write_brief force-verifies anything left unjudged
8. brief writer turns the verified ledger + master's synthesis notes into the 8-section brief; re-runs auto-diff against the prior dated run
9. deliverables: brief.md, claims.json (with timings and corrections log), filterable claims-report.html
10. eval harness grades the run (structure, grounding, judge, latency); failures loop back as fixes
11. audit history stores every exchange per brand; brand threads resume later with conversation + ledger loaded
